column1: # How people actually type Kannada in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# Two kinds of spelling are here, and neither is reachable from the phonetic
#  - Words the rules get wrong because Latin spelling does not carry the
#    difference: a long vowel nobody doubles ("nanu" is ನಾನು, "hogu" is ಹೋಗು),
#    retroflex against dental ("madu" is ಮಾಡು, "oota" is ಊಟ), ಳ and ಣ typed
#    as plain l and n ("helu" ಹೇಳು, "anna" ಅಣ್ಣ), a geminate typed single
#    ("gothu" ಗೊತ್ತು), aspirates the rules read plain ("athava" ಅಥವಾ).
#  - Spoken forms chat writes as they sound, which the formal word list lacks:
# The rules already handle th → ತ, sht → ಷ್ಟ, -galu → -ಗಳು, -agi → -ಾಗಿ,
# ol → ಒಳ, -ona → -ಓಣ, a two-syllable "e" read long (beku ಬೇಕು) and more;
# words they get right are left out. A hand-written draft of the commonest few
# hundred words; it wants a Kannada speaker's review.
# Format: spelling<TAB>kannada   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
# Loaded after en_kn.tsv, so the hand-written loanword spellings win a tie.
